position: STAY on Bunny behind the existing VideoProvider seam. Do not write transcoding or delivery. Spend ~1.5 engineer-months hardening the seam into a real exit ramp (per-row provider dispatch, a driver-agnostic conformance suite, de-leaking two provider assumptions that escaped the seam) and on the two Bunny settings that cost more per month than any provider change (unmetered 4K minutes, keep-originals + MP4 fallback). Add capabilities as pre/post-processing around the seam, and a second driver only when a named trigger fires.
summary: Bunny is 9% of revenue at the six-month target (₹29,689 of ₹3,30,000, docs/SCALE-PLAN.md:26-36) — smaller than the Vercel+Supabase fixed floor of ₹25,785 in the same table. Self-hosting cannot address the larger half, and it does not win on the smaller half at any scale this business will reach: cost.json finds no breakeven inside 10–1,000 weddings/month once one on-call human is priced, and infra-only crossing needs ~900–1,000/month on the R2 stack. The decision is therefore not 'is transcoding hard' (it is) but 'what does ₹6–9 lakh of build and ₹35k–4 lakh/month of standing ops buy' — and the honest answer at 10 weddings/month is that it buys a ₹7,534 line item you were going to keep paying anyway, plus a wedding-night pager. Meanwhile the seam that makes this reversible already exists and is already exercised by a second full driver in production code: lib/video/provider.ts:71-126 stops every Bunny type at the file, lib/video/index.ts:10-14 is the one switch, and lib/video/fake.ts:20-142 is a complete non-Bunny implementation that CI, Playwright and the offline demo run against. Writing a third implementation is a known shape, not a rewrite — which is exactly why it should be deferred until a trigger, not done on suspicion. The lock-in that actually exists is not the five methods. It is the bytes (₹11k of egress to leave today, ₹65k at the 60/month run rate, 3–4× that if originals are kept), the absolute b-cdn.net hostnames baked into every photos.url row, and — the longest pole by far — the accumulated operational knowledge in scripts/verify-bunny-playback.ts, scripts/verify-upload-resume.ts and scripts/preflight.ts, each assertion of which exists because it caught a real bug that a fresh pipeline would have to rediscover.
architecture: Unchanged shape, three additions. (1) Keep VideoProvider (lib/video/provider.ts) as the only place a video platform is named; keep PhotoProvider likewise. (2) Wire the per-row escape hatch that is already half-built: titles.provider is persisted (lib/schema.ts:436) and seed rows already carry 'fake' (lib/db/seed-data.ts:163), but nothing dispatches on it — getVideoProvider() reads env only. Make it getVideoProvider(title.provider), ~10 lines, and a future driver can take new uploads while every existing film keeps playing from Bunny. That converts a big-bang migration into a per-upload cutover with no backfill on the critical path. (3) Capabilities are added as pre/post-processing around the seam, never inside the driver: client-side or Lambda-style pre-transcode (proxy generation, a bitrate ladder decision, watermarking) runs before createUpload; anything Bunny will not do to a finished asset (a signed download, a re-mux, an archive copy pushed to B2 cold storage) hangs off getDownloadUrl and getStatus. Delivery stays on Bunny's Standard tier — 119 PoPs with Indian presence is what the sub-1.5s-on-4G promise in CLAUDE.md's definition of done actually rests on, and no self-hosted alternative in cost.json beats $0.030/GB with Indian PoPs (CloudFront India is 3.6×; Cloudflare is $0 only if its own video-delivery policy page is wrong).
benefits: Zero build cost against the rival's 8–12 engineer-weeks (cost.json assumptions[13], ₹6–9 lakh at Indian contract rates) for a pipeline that reaches parity with what Bunny gives free — standard encoding to 1080p costs $0 on Bunny (bunny.net/docs/stream/pricing).

Zero dedicated ops headcount. The failure modes are already covered without a human: app/api/cron/reconcile/route.ts:14-124 settles anything the webhook lost and emails ops the moment it has to, and app/api/cron/synthetic/route.ts:52-91 walks a real guest's path hourly. cost.json prices the self-hosted alternative's cheapest honest cover at ₹35,000/month today rising to ₹4,00,000 — larger than the entire Bunny bill until ~300 weddings/month.

The seam is proven, not asserted. lib/video/fake.ts:20-142 is a complete second VideoProvider — TUS ticket, status timer, playback, webhook signer — that CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:14-18), the Playwright suite and an offline planner demo run against. The claim 'a self-hosted driver is a new implementation and one line in lib/video/index.ts' has been executed once already.

Nothing outside the seam names Bunny in a load-bearing way: no Bunny hostname, type or API shape appears anywhere in app/, components/, modules/ or themes/ except one comment, one privacy disclosure (app/privacy/page.tsx:40), the webhook route's own path, and the two leaks listed under costs. next.config.ts:30-33's '**.b-cdn.net' is one line.

Delivery economics do not improve by self-hosting. Bunny's marginal cost per wedding at list is $7.87, of which $2.57 is delivery at India-PoP rates (cost.json breakeven). The only line self-hosting removes cleanly is 4K premium encoding at $0.15/min — and that line is currently unenforced in code (nothing under lib/, app/ or components/ sets enabledResolutions), so it is cheaper to cap it than to replace the vendor.

Exit price is bounded and known. Moving every stored byte out today costs ~3,800 GB × $0.03 = ₹10,910 of egress; at the 60-weddings-per-month steady state, ₹65,470 (3–4× if keep-originals stays on). A reversible ₹11k decision does not justify a ₹6–9 lakh irreversible one.

Storage price risk — the one input that compounds and is outside our control (docs/PRICING.md:276-294) — is hedged more cheaply by moving originals to B2 at $6.95/TB behind getDownloadUrl than by replacing the whole pipeline, because that is a pre/post-processing step at the seam and needs no transcoder at all.
costs_and_losses: Single-vendor concentration is real and not mitigated by a seam: Bunny is transcode, video CDN, photo origin and photo CDN simultaneously. app/api/cron/synthetic/route.ts:29-31 deliberately stops at minting a token and does not fetch the manifest, so a Bunny edge fault on a wedding evening is invisible to our own alerting by design.

Per-catalogue delivery stays an estimate forever. lib/video/bunny.ts:234-262 derives deliveredGb from watchTimeChart × GB_PER_HOUR.standard (2.15, lib/entitlements.ts:131, itself marked a placeholder) because Bunny reports bandwidth only per pull zone. A self-hosted origin would get real per-object bytes from CDN logs. Anyone capacity-planning or billing off usage_rollup.delivered_gb today is billing off an assumption — that is a genuine, permanent loss from staying.

Two provider assumptions have escaped the seam and would silently break a swap. modules/curated-row/Guest.tsx:27-29 hard-codes 'preview.webp' because Bunny happens to write an animated preview beside the poster; components/streaming/useHlsPlayback.ts:123-136 re-appends '?token=&expires=' to every child URL under signedPrefix, which is coupled to directory-style query signing, not merely to Bunny. Both are small; both are exactly the kind of thing that turns a one-line switch into a two-week debug.

The Bunny webhook URL is an account-key-gated dashboard setting this repo cannot read, verify or change. scripts/preflight.ts checks every other Bunny setting and not this one, and a domain switchover already left it pointed at a dead alias once (docs/GO-LIVE.md:213-244). Staying means keeping an un-automatable manual step in every domain change.

app/api/cron/usage/route.ts:56-69 makes two sequential Bunny API calls per title per night inside one serverless invocation with no maxDuration and no resume (verified real in verify-scalability.json). That is a coupling to Bunny's per-video API shape that bites regardless of provider and gets worse linearly with the library.

photos.url stores absolute b-cdn.net URLs (scripts/repoint-photo-cdn.ts's own header: 'the one resource whose old name is visible to guests, in the host of every photograph URL'). A future host change is a row rewrite, not a config change — the script exists, but it must be run, by hand, and is not wired into any deploy step.

Bunny's photo pull zone has no token authentication at all (N-83, map §7.2) — lib/photos/bunny.ts never signs. Staying does not create this, but it means the fix has to be built on Bunny's signing model rather than designed in from scratch.
risks: Storage price is the one cost that compounds and is outside our control. docs/PRICING.md:291-294 shows long-term Cinema at 17% margin breaking even at a 1.2× storage price — a 20% Bunny rise erases the row entirely, and it is prepaid so it cannot be repriced. This is the single strongest argument the rival has, and it is real.

Keep-originals and MP4 fallback are ON (lib/video/bunny.ts:198-201, checked against the account API). cost.json assumptions[4] notes this multiplies the storage line 3–4× over the ladder-only model both sides were compared on. That means today's Bunny bill is materially higher than SCALE-PLAN's table implies — and it is a setting, not a vendor problem.

The 4K premium-encoding allowance is policy, not code. Nothing under lib/, app/ or components/ sets enabledResolutions; resolutions are a library-wide Bunny setting. At 1,000 weddings/month that unmetered line is ₹1,43,550/month (cost.json assumptions[6]). An uncapped exposure is a worse risk than a vendor.

Bunny has no Indian origin — the photo zone is in Singapore (lib/photos/bunny.ts:16-17) and Mumbai is 'planned' on the storage pricing page. A data-residency requirement from a studio contract or DPDP rules would force a move on a timeline we do not control.
Concentration risk compounds with the exit price: every month on Bunny adds stored bytes, so the cost of leaving rises linearly while the probability of wanting to leave does not fall.

Deferring the second driver risks the seam rotting. Two leaks already escaped it (curated-row, useHlsPlayback). Without a conformance suite that runs against a non-Bunny driver, 'the seam holds' becomes an untested claim — the same way driver parity between MemoryRepository and SupabaseRepository was an untested claim until it turned out to be false (map §7.1).
triggers_to_revisit: Sustained ≥300 weddings/month. cost.json puts infra-only crossing at ~900–1,000/month on the R2 stack and ~50–60 on the B2 stack, but 300 is where the delivery volume (26 TB/month) makes both a Bunny committed contract and a serious self-host study worth an engineer's time — and it is also where SCALE-PLAN §3 says Vercel's own function ceiling arrives, so the whole stack gets re-decided together.

Bunny raises storage above ₹1.14/GB-month (a 20% rise from today's ₹0.95). docs/PRICING.md:294 states plainly that this erases the long-term Cinema margin. Revisit on the announcement, not after the invoice.

Bunny refuses a committed contract past 10 TB/month, or offers worse than list minus 20%. SCALE-PLAN §5 already says to open that conversation; a refusal is the clearest possible signal that list price is the ceiling of the relationship.

Premium 4K encoding exceeds ~₹50,000/month. That is the one line self-hosting removes cleanly, and past that figure a GPU box pays for itself on encoding alone — but only after the allowance has been enforced in code and the number is real rather than an unenforced policy estimate.
A contract or regulation requires video origin storage inside India, or requires DRM / forensic watermarking Bunny does not offer. Neither is buyable from Bunny today.

Per-catalogue delivery must be measured rather than derived — e.g. because a studio disputes an overage bill or a plan is priced on delivered GB. Bunny cannot supply it; a self-hosted origin can. Until someone disputes a bill, this is a nicety.
Two consecutive Bunny incidents that reach a wedding audience. The trigger is customer-visible impact, not uptime-page colour.
migration_path: Week 1 — Wire the escape hatch that is already half-built: change getVideoProvider() in lib/video/index.ts to accept a provider name and dispatch on titles.provider (persisted at lib/schema.ts:436, already carrying 'fake' in lib/db/seed-data.ts:163). Ten lines. This converts any future move from a big-bang migration plus byte backfill into a per-upload cutover where old films keep playing from Bunny indefinitely.

Week 2 — De-leak the seam. Replace the hard-coded 'preview.webp' in modules/curated-row/Guest.tsx:27-29 with a nullable previewFile on AssetStatus that the driver supplies, and move the token-reappending logic in components/streaming/useHlsPlayback.ts:123-136 behind a driver-supplied signing hint on PlaybackTicket rather than a URL-prefix string match.

Weeks 3-4 — Generalise the proof. Turn scripts/verify-bunny-playback.ts into `pnpm verify:provider`, driver-agnostic, asserting the six properties that have each caught a real bug: signed manifest, signed child playlist, signed poster, all three refused unsigned, hls.js reaching decoded frames, and TUS offset resume after a network drop (scripts/verify-upload-resume.ts). Run it against FakeVideoProvider in CI. That suite is the real deliverable of any future migration and it costs one week now instead of three later.

Week 5 — Cap the unmetered line. Enforce the 4K/premium allowance at upload rather than as a library-wide Bunny setting: set enabledResolutions per asset at createUpload from the catalogue's plan (Cinema vs Deliver/Keep, lib/entitlements.ts). This is the single largest cost line self-hosting was going to remove, removed without changing vendor.

Week 6 — Decide keep-originals and MP4 fallback (lib/video/bunny.ts:198-201). If originals must be kept for the 'originals downloadable untouched' promise, move them off Bunny Stream to Backblaze B2 at $6.95/TB behind getDownloadUrl as a post-processing step at the seam — the archive copy needs no transcoder, no CDN and no on-call. This is worth more per month than any provider change and is the honest hedge against the storage-price risk in docs/PRICING.md:291.
Week 7 — Fix the Bunny API coupling that bites regardless: batch and paginate app/api/cron/usage/route.ts:56-69's per-title sequential provider calls, with a resume cursor and maxDuration.

Week 8 — Open the committed-contract conversation with Bunny as soon as delivery passes 10 TB/month (SCALE-PLAN §5). A negotiated rate pushes every breakeven in cost.json further out at zero engineering cost.

On a trigger, not before — Build SelfHostedVideoProvider against the interface, run `pnpm verify:provider` against it until green, then route new uploads to it by writing titles.provider='self' while every existing film continues to serve from Bunny. Backfill old assets only if and when the egress is cheaper than the remaining Bunny storage bill. No flag day, no rewrite, and the decision stays reversible in both directions.
what_it_does_not_fix: None of the actual production defects. SupabaseRepository silently ignores the liveOnly/live_at publish gate for both titles and photographs (lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1390-1396 and :1625-1631, verified real) — guests see unpublished content in production today. That is a repository bug, not a video bug, and it is strictly more urgent than any provider decision.
The Vercel+Supabase fixed floor, which is ₹25,785 of the ₹55,474 six-month infra total (docs/SCALE-PLAN.md:26-36) — more than half of infra, and untouched by anything a transcoder does.
Per-object delivery metering. deliveredGb stays derived from watch time × an assumed bitrate (lib/video/bunny.ts:234-262, lib/entitlements.ts:131).
The photo pull zone's total lack of token authentication (N-83) — that is a separate, already-scoped piece of work on lib/photos/bunny.ts.

The 60-day GitHub Actions scheduler self-disable that silently stops four of six cron jobs, including every alert path (verify-deployability.json, real=true, severity high). That is where a wedding-night failure actually comes from.
The webhook-URL blind spot: it stays a manual, account-key-gated dashboard setting whatever the driver is — though a self-hosted pipeline would remove it, which is a fair point for the rival.

Any Startup India grant narrative. If the motive for writing a transcoder is a grant story rather than economics, the grant is cheaper to earn on the product surfaces (themes, direct-to-client) than on infrastructure a vendor already sells at a loss-leading price.
evidence: lib/video/provider.ts:1-8 — the interface's own header: 'Switching from Bunny to Cloudflare is a new implementation of this interface and one line in lib/video/index.ts — the decision in doc 05 is explicitly a default, not a lock-in.'

lib/video/provider.ts:71-126 — the whole VideoProvider surface: createUpload, getPlaybackToken, getStatus, getAssetUrl, getDownloadUrl, deleteAsset, getUsage, verifyWebhook. No Bunny type crosses this file.
lib/video/index.ts:10-14 — the one switch on provider in the codebase; lib/video/index.ts:16-18 setVideoProvider for injection.
lib/video/fake.ts:20-142 — a complete second driver, not a mock; .github/workflows/ci.yml:14-18 runs the whole suite against it.

lib/schema.ts:436 — titles.provider persisted per row, default 'bunny'; lib/db/seed-data.ts:163 already carries 'fake'. Nothing dispatches on it yet (getVideoProvider takes no argument) — the per-row exit ramp is stored but unwired.
lib/video/bunny.ts:198-201 — keep-originals and MP4 fallback are ON, checked against the account API; this is the largest single lever on the storage bill and it is a setting.
lib/video/bunny.ts:234-262 — deliveredGb derived from watchTimeChart × GB_PER_HOUR.standard because Bunny reports bandwidth only per pull zone; lib/entitlements.ts:131 marks 2.15 a placeholder.
lib/video/bunny.ts:96-148 — directory-scoped signing, verified live by pnpm verify:playback; the constraint any replacement origin must reproduce.
components/streaming/useHlsPlayback.ts:123-136 — xhrSetup re-appends '?token=&expires=' to child URLs under signedPrefix; coupled to query-string directory signing, a leak outside the seam.
modules/curated-row/Guest.tsx:27-29 — 'preview.webp' hard-coded because Bunny writes an animated preview beside the poster; the second leak outside the seam.
next.config.ts:30-33 — images.remotePatterns '**.b-cdn.net'; one line, the only infrastructure hostname in app configuration.
scripts/repoint-photo-cdn.ts:17-20 — 'photos.url stores an absolute URL'; the photo zone is the one Bunny resource whose name is visible to guests, and a rehost script already exists.
app/api/cron/usage/route.ts:56-69 — nested sequential provider.getUsage per title in one invocation, no maxDuration, no resume (confirmed in verify-scalability.json).

app/api/cron/reconcile/route.ts:14-124 and app/api/cron/synthetic/route.ts:52-91 — the unattended ops surface that today replaces a self-hosted pipeline's on-call rota; synthetic deliberately stops at the token (:29-31).
lib/env.ts:215-230 — four Bunny vars are required at boot when VIDEO_DRIVER=bunny; the configuration surface a second driver must replace is four keys, not a system.

docs/SCALE-PLAN.md:26-36 — 60 weddings / six months: revenue ₹3,30,000, Bunny ₹29,689 (storage ₹6,351 + delivery ₹14,743 + 4K encoding ₹8,595), Vercel+Supabase ₹25,785, infra 16.8%. Bunny is 9.0% of revenue; the untouchable fixed floor is larger than the addressable line.

docs/PRICING.md:291-294 — long-term Cinema 5 yr at 17% margin, breakeven at 1.2× storage price, prepaid and unrepriceable. The strongest real argument for controlling storage — which is answered by cold-storing originals, not by writing a transcoder.

cost.json 'breakeven' — no breakeven inside 10–1,000 weddings/month once people are priced; infra-only crossing at ~900–1,000/month (R2) or ~50–60/month (B2, storage-only saving); at 1,000/month the closest case is ₹7.86 lakh self-hosted vs ₹7.53 lakh Bunny at list, before any negotiated contract.

cost.json scenarios[0] — at today's 10 weddings/month: Bunny ₹7,534 vs self-hosted ₹19,971 infra + ₹35,000 people = 7.3× dearer. The fixed floor of a two-box pipeline already exceeds the entire Bunny bill.

cost.json assumptions[13] — one-off build 8–12 engineer-weeks / ₹6–9 lakh, and it must reproduce the TUS offset resume that components/admin/UploadManager.tsx:67-83 relies on, which CLAUDE.md names as the place the schedule slips.

cost.json assumptions[10] — the two unpriced self-host risks that would decide it: Cloudflare's own policy page restricts self-serve CDN video delivery, and neither R2, B2 nor Hetzner has an Indian origin, against a product promise of 1.5s first play on 4G.

verify-scalability.json and verify-deployability.json (real=true) — the confirmed defects are the Supabase liveOnly gap, the heartbeat cost, unpaginated reads, and four of six crons on a scheduler that self-disables after 60 days. None is a video-provider problem.
https://bunny.net/docs/stream/pricing — storage $0.01/GB-month, Standard delivery Asia & Oceania $0.030/GB, standard encoding free, premium 2160p/1440p $0.150/min (fetched 15 Sep 2026).
https://bunny.net/pricing/storage/ — Bunny Edge Storage regions; Mumbai listed as 'planned', i.e. no Indian origin today.

https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/reference/policies-compliances/delivering-videos-with-cloudflare/ — video via CDN restricted to Stream / Stream Delivery (Enterprise) on self-serve plans, which is the load-bearing assumption under the rival's cheapest delivery line.
https://aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/pricing/pay-as-you-go/ — CloudFront India $0.109/GB (next 9 TB), $0.085 (next 40 TB): 2.8–3.6× Bunny's Asia rate, so the India-PoP alternative never wins on price.
https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing — B2 $6.95/TB-month with free egress to Bunny under the Bandwidth Alliance: the cheap hedge on storage that needs no transcoder and no vendor change.
https://github.com/tus/tusd — the reference TUS server a self-hosted ingest would start from; free, but it is the start of the 8–12 weeks, not the end.
